#1048. Architecture of a portal complex embedded in the poxvirus core

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

We’re sharing this article early to provide faster access to peer-reviewed, accepted research. It is citable and carries a permanent DOI. This version is subject to further edits and will be replaced automatically by the final Version of Record. All legal disclaimers apply.

Gene transcription within the viral core is a distinctive feature of poxvirus replication. Following entry into the cytoplasm, the poxvirus core dissociates from the lateral bodies and undergoes expansion, functioning as a compartment for early transcription1. However, how molecules are exchanged between the viral core and the host cytoplasm remains poorly understood. Here, using cryo-electron tomography and sub-tomogram averaging, we determine the structures of the portal complex and its central pore on the vaccinia virus core at 6.7 Å and 4.4 Å resolution, respectively. Guided by structural predictions and experimental density, we identify three viral proteins, E8, E6 and L3, as the principal components of the pore and construct a structural model of their organization. The pore contains a narrow, positively charged constriction formed by conserved lysine residues in L3, substitutions of which impair viral gene expression and propagation. The dimensions and electrostatic properties of the channel are consistent with a potential role in molecular exchange across the core wall. Together, our findings establish a structural framework for understanding the organization and potential function of the poxvirus portal complex.

#1047. FA chair to examine Gianni Infantino’s Fifa World Cup sell-off plan documents

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Gianni Infantino was forced to abandon his controversial plan earlier this year

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt is set to inspect documentation in person regarding Fifa’s deeply contentious World Cup private investment proposal, it is understood.

The global governing body dispatched a letter on 2 November to members of the Fifa Council – where Hewitt serves as a Fifa vice-president – offering them the opportunity to examine the files at its headquarters in Zurich.

Hewitt is believed to have taken up the offer, though a firm date for the trip remains unconfirmed. Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin is likewise thought to have agreed to attend.

Relations between Uefa and Fifa president Gianni Infantino broke down over the project, which involved creating a new entity named Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) to manage commercial and operational activities for both the men’s and women’s World Cups alongside other Fifa tournaments.

Under the blueprint, a minority shareholding in FFE was to be acquired by private investors, led by Thrive Capital, an entity established by Joshua Kushner, whose brother is the son-in-law of United States President Donald Trump.

The initiative was ultimately scrapped following opposition from Uefa and a pair of other continental confederations.

Hewitt’s career experience in private equity provides her with direct insight into the standard documentation and financial details expected in proposals of this nature.

Fifa issued the invitation after European representatives on the Fifa Council sent a formal letter on 19 October requesting clarity on several matters, including the FFE arrangement and disciplinary proceedings involving Folarin Balogun.

Provisions regarding non-disclosure agreements and the specific terms governing document inspection in Zurich have yet to be finalised.

Earlier on Tuesday, the French Football Federation formally endorsed Philippe Diallo’s bid for the Fifa presidency.

On Monday, Uefa confirmed that the 63-year-old had secured the support of national association delegates across its executive committee and the Fifa Council to challenge Infantino.

Disquiet over the FFE proposals prompted European football’s governing body to promise in August that it would put forward a credible challenger to Infantino.

Diallo’s domestic federation has now unanimously backed his campaign, stating: "World football is going through a pivotal period in its history. The challenges affecting its governance demand clear thinking and responsibility.

"Restoring trust, preserving the universality of football, rebuilding Fifa’s credibility, and placing the development of football in all regions of the world at the heart of its actions are essential issues for the entire international football community.

"By accepting this invitation, Philippe Diallo is responding to a desire to open a new chapter for the governance of world football."

Figures within Uefa had previously hoped that former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, who currently serves as Fifa’s chief of global football development, might enter the race, though he is believed to have declined the prospect last week.

#1045. Ecclestone ruled out of WBBL

Adelaide Strikers announced on Tuesday that England spinner Sophie Ecclestone would be ruled out for the remainder of the WBBL season; it comes as Issy Wong has been withdrawn from England A's squad to take on India A in a multi-format series

Sophie Ecclestone has been ruled out of the remainder of the WBBL season due to a back injury.

Adelaide Strikers revealed the England spinner picked the injury prior to their match against the Perth Scorchers.

After undergoing scans, the England and Wales Cricket Board and the Strikers determined in consultation that Ecclestone would "require a period of rehabilitation".

Ecclestone, who has taken four wickets in four matches for the Strikers in the WBBL this season with an economy of 7.62, said she was devastated her season has come to an end prematurely.

"I've loved my time in Adelaide and with the Strikers, and I'll be supporting the team every step of the way for the remainder of the season," she said.

"Our squad has produced some incredible performances this year, and I'll be cheering the girls on as they push for finals."

It comes as a huge blow for the Strikers, who are already without fast bowler Darcie Brown, who has also been sidelined with a back injury.

Strikers coach Luke Williams said: "Sophie has been an incredible addition to the Strikers, not only with her batting and bowling, but also through her leadership and experience.

"She is one of the world's premier bowlers and, while we're disappointed to lose her, we're incredibly grateful for everything she has contributed during her time at the club.

"We wish Sophie all the very best with her recovery and look forward to welcoming her back to Adelaide in the future."

Wong, Lamb withdrawn from England A squads

Issy Wong has been withdrawn from England A's multi-format tour of India due to a stress fracture in her right foot.

She'll be replaced by Alexa Stonehouse for the four-day squad, while no replacement for Wong has been called up for the white-ball matches.

Lancashire's Emma Lamb has undergone surgery on a back injury and has subsequently been withdrawn from the 50-over and four-day squads.

She is replaced by 19-year-old Durham batting all-rounder Grace Thompson.

The forward England star will be in attendance at the London Playing Fields Foundation’s prestigious ‘Made in London Award’ at its Gala Dinner at The Savoy on November 19

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Former England and Chelsea star Joe Cole has highlighted the vital importance of protecting grassroots pitches across the capital, warning "you can’t produce any footballers without football pitches."

The 45-year-old enjoyed an illustrious playing career, which included three Premier League titles at Stamford Bridge and 56 caps for the Three Lions, and London’s local playing fields played a pivotal role in shaping his journey to the top.

Established in 1890, the charity works to safeguard the capital’s green spaces, inspiring future generations to follow in the footsteps of sporting greats. Speaking exclusively to FourFourTwo, Cole admitted the nomination means a great deal to him.

"London and football are two of the things most dearest to my heart," Cole said. "I’m a London kid. I was born in Camden Town, and obviously football is my passion, so the two things together make perfect sense, and they do a great job there.

"We need to protect the green space, not just for football, but for every sport, for kids to play, particularly in London. We have a rich history of producing footballers. You can’t produce any footballers without football pitches – whether that be five-a-side, seven-a-side, 11-a-side, cricket pitches, anything for young people to go out and be active. It’s about keeping them off the developers and making sure there’s room for kids to play."

Renowned throughout his career for his street-footballer flair and close control, Cole honed his trademark skills growing up in north London during the 1980s, making the most of whatever space was available.

"I lived in a ground-floor flat with a tiny garden, so London was my back garden," Cole recalled. "There were no boundaries. There was a bit of grass right outside my house, a wall, and over the back end there was a little concrete seven-a-side pitch.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

"You had to be imaginative. I used to walk to Market Road, which was one of the first AstroTurf pitches in the country. London is just a city riddled with little areas to play. I love London, I really do, and I can’t ever see myself living far from it."To learn more about the London Playing Fields Foundation visit lpff.org.uk

#1043. JJ Gabriel posts farewell message to Man United ahead of proposed Real Madrid move

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

JJ Gabriel has been heavily linked with a move to Real Madrid

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Teenage wonderkid JJ Gabriel has appeared to confirm his Manchester United exit in a video posted on social media.

The 16-year-old, who has never played a competitive match for the first team, joined United as a 10-year-old in 2020.

He has been absent from the club since requesting in September that his registration be cancelled, shortly before his 16th birthday on 6 October.

Gabriel made no mention of where he intends to go next, but widespread speculation has linked him with Real Madrid, and his goodbye video on Instagram appears to have edged him closer to a move to the Spanish giants.

Gabriel said in his video: “Dear Manchester United, I arrived in 2020 as a 10-year-old boy with big dreams. Here I grew as a player and a person. From scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy Award.

“You gave me moments I will always treasure. To every coach and every member of staff, to my team-mates and everyone who supported me, thank you for believing in me and helping me grow.

“As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be a part of my story. Thank you for everything, JJ.”

The teenager is the son of former Republic of Ireland international Joe O’Cearuill.

Last season he became the youngest ever winner of United’s Jimmy Murphy Award, given to the club’s young player of the year.

Despite his absence, Gabriel had remained registered to United, who the Press Association understands are ready to explore legal options against the youngster’s next club over possible broken regulations.

United had initially hoped to persuade him to stay.

It now appears his hat-trick against Sabah on his Uefa Youth League debut on September 10 will be his final appearance for the club.

Gabriel shone in the 5-0 victory, but his representatives were disappointed he was not registered to play later that day in the Champions League fixture against the champions of Azerbaijan.

He had been due to appear in the Carabao Cup tie against Brighton the following week, but had upped sticks by that point.

Had he featured in that tie, Gabriel would have become the club’s youngest player in a competitive match, having already appeared off the bench for Michael Carrick’s side in an August friendly against Atletico Madrid.

England's next generation came of age at the Metropolitano on Sunday night

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Succession planning is one of international football’s trickiest arts, especially when replacing a goalkeeper who has laid claim to the No. 1 shirt for nearly a decade, or trying to fix a left-back spot that has become something of a revolving door.

For Thomas Tuchel, though, the answers to two of England’s biggest long-term headaches have been forged at Elland Road and St James’ Park.

On a thrilling Sunday night in Madrid, as 10-man England stunned reigning world champions Spain 3-2 to snap La Roja’s 43-match unbeaten run, Leeds United’s James Trafford and Newcastle’s Lewis Hall announced themselves as the next generation of Three Lions stalwarts.

For almost 10 years, Jordan Pickford’s status as England’s undisputed No. 1 has been largely uninterrupted, stretching from the 2018 World Cup to last summer’s semi-final run in North America. It left little room for an understudy to build experience or a case for selection.

Moving on from a 94-cap mainstay is never straightforward, which is why Trafford’s decision to swap Manchester City’s bench for regular Premier League football at Leeds in August has proven so vital for Tuchel. Playing week-in, week-out has helped the 24-year-old develop into a ready-made alternative capable of taking the gloves whenever Pickford eventually hangs his up.

Handed a rare start at the Metropolitano and given the chance to test his temperament and big-game mentality against elite opposition, Trafford watched as goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White fired England into a 3-0 lead.

But when Elliot Anderson saw red in the 62nd minute, Leeds’ No.1 was faced with a relentless Spanish siege. Spain racked up 23 shots, seven on target and 2.73 Expected Goals (xG), yet Trafford refused to buckle.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

The Leeds stopper made five crucial saves - repelling Fermin Lopez from close range, recovering well to deny Lamine Yamal and Marc Cucurella, and producing an outstanding stoppage-time double save to thwart Yamal and Aymeric Laporte - all the while impressing Tuchel with his composure during build-up.

At left-back, Tuchel’s gratitude to Newcastle should be equally clear. Since Euro 2024, England have cycled through 10 different players in the role, experimenting with the likes of Nico O’Reilly and Myles Lewis-Skelly, right-footed deputies such as Djed Spence, and stopgaps. This is largely because nobody had convincingly locked down the position consistently at club level.

Many felt Hall was unfairly overlooked when Tuchel left him out of the 2026 World Cup squad, a tournament in which England’s left flank seemed to lack balance. But the 22-year-old’s emergence as an indispensable starter for Newcastle, particularly this season, has finally given Tuchel a specialist he can rely on.

Against one of the most dangerous wingers on the planet, Lamine Yamal, Hall was excellent. Defensively, he registered five clearances and two vital first-half interventions inside his own box to snuff out Yamal and Mikel Merino, before drawing two late fouls to relieve pressure in the dying seconds.

In possession, he was just as accomplished, completing five dribbles in the first half alone - more than Spain’s entire 10 outfield players combined. He found a teammate with 30 of his 34 passes (88 per cent accuracy), providing natural left-footed width that facilitated Anthony Gordon's strong performance, too.

Pickford’s experience ensures he won't be surrendering his place without a fight, and Tuchel insisted afterwards that no permanent changing of the guard has taken place. International bosses are ultimately reliant on club environments to forge their stars, so by entrusting Trafford and Hall with pivotal Premier League roles, Leeds and Newcastle are doing the heavy lifting for future tournaments.

Joe joined FourFourTwo as senior digital writer in July 2025 after five years covering Leeds United in the Championship and Premier League. #1041. Northern Ireland earn remarkable promotion to Nations League top tier

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Hungary 1-1 Northern Ireland: Justin Devenny’s superb strike in Budapest earned the visitors they needed to top Group B2, just two years after earning promotion from League C

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Justin Devenny’s superb strike saw Northern Ireland earn promotion to the top flight of the Nations League with a hard-fought 1-1 draw away to closest challengers Hungary in Budapest.

Barnabas Varga ended Northern Ireland’s proud record of not having conceded in this campaign when he fired the hosts in front after 35 minutes – a goal that also sent Hungary to the top of the group.

But moments after Isaac Price had hit the post for Michael O’Neill’s young side, Devenny smashed the ball into the top left-hand corner in the 65th minute to restore Northern Ireland’s one-point advantage as group leaders.

The visitors were on the back foot for much of the first half, with Hungary captain Dominik Szoboszlai hitting the post, but Michael O’Neill, serving a touchline ban in the stands as former captain Steven Davis led things from the touchline, orchestrated key substitutions.

Northern Ireland started with Patrick Kelly in place of the suspended Jamie Donley up front but brought on Josh Magennis at half-time before Kieran Morrison and Brodie Spencer soon followed to help the visitors become a much greater threat going forward.

Magennis’ physical presence and the extra pace paid dividends as, just two years after earning promotion from League C, Northern Ireland completed an unbeaten campaign in Group B2 to secure their place at the top table of European football.

Without Donley, the lack of a clear outlet told in a first half which saw Hungary come forward time and again.

There was a big panic five minutes in following an uncharacteristic mistake from Pierce Charles, whose pass went straight to Bendeguez Bolla, a late change to the Hungary side who whipped in a superb low cross from which skipper Szoboszlai struck the post.

Northern Ireland were pegged back but might have snatched the lead from a Ciaron Brown long throw in the 33rd minute. However Tom Atcheson did not seem to realise how much space he had as he prodded a weak shot towards his Blackburn team-mate Balazs Toth.

Two minutes later Pierce Charles launched a long free-kick into the box. Brown went down under an Andras Schafer challenge but as Northern Ireland appealed in vain for a penalty, Toth kicked it long. Trai Hume got his head to the ball but could not get it as far as Pierce Charles, allowing Varga to nip in and score.

O’Neill will have felt the frustration of his ban with his side trailing at half-time, but his changes worked regardless.

Terry Devlin, the matchwinner on Saturday, had already fired into the side-netting before Price’s low strike from the edge of the box cannoned back off the post.

Four minutes later they were level. Hume’s long throw almost fell for Shea Charles but instead sat up for Devenny to take a touch before thumping an unstoppable strike into the top corner.

As time ticked down, Hungary pushed forward in increasing desperation – with Rajmund Toth firing over late on – but Northern Ireland dug in with the defensive resilience which has been the cornerstone of this campaign.
